title: NXT ResolveDesk
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: convention-honoring (probability 0.4)
Title: NXT ResolveDesk
Thesis: A unified agent console surfacing live Shopify order, inventory, and refund data inline so reps resolve escalations without tab-switching.
Why this frame: This is the workflow any competent CX-tooling designer would build: a single-pane agent desktop wrapping Shopify Admin APIs. It is the strong, defensible baseline that wins on throughput and trust.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Maya Torres
  Role: Tier-2 Retail Customer Service Representative
  Context: Handles 40+ escalated tickets a day across chat and email for a mid-market Shopify Plus apparel brand; works a 8-hour shift with a 9-minute average handle time target and an SLA of first-response under 4 hours.
  Emotional state: Time-pressured and context-starved — fluent at empathy but exhausted by tab-switching between Shopify Admin, the helpdesk, the 3PL portal, and a refund spreadsheet.
  Pain points:
    - Pivoting across 5+ browser tabs to assemble one customer's full story before she can even reply
    - Refund status lag — she promises a refund 'processed' that Shopify hasn't actually settled, generating a second angry ticket
    - No inline visibility into live inventory, so substitution offers are guesses that bounce back out-of-stock
    - Manual copy-paste of order numbers and tracking links invites transcription errors and policy missteps
  JTBD: When an escalated product complaint lands in my queue, I want every relevant Shopify fact and a vetted resolution in one screen, so I can fix it correctly on the first reply without breaking policy or re-opening the ticket.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - CX Team Lead: Monitors queue health, approves goodwill credits above $50, reviews audit trail for compliance
  - Tier-3 Specialist: Receives structured handoffs for fraud, chargebacks, and complex multi-order disputes
  - Fulfillment / 3PL Coordinator: Confirms warehouse holds and re-ships triggered by agent actions via webhook
  - End Customer: Receives the resolution, refund confirmation, or substitution offer across their original channel
  - Finance / Refund Approver: Auto-notified when cumulative refunds per order exceed configured thresholds

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Mid-shift, Maya opens an angry escalation about a delayed refund. The Unified Context Panel loads order history, live refund settlement status, and inventory in under two seconds; an AI-drafted resolution sits ready, she edits one sentence, clicks Resolve, and watches the refund issue, the customer email send, and the audit trail stamp — all without leaving the screen.

USE CASES (12) - the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Damaged-item refund resolution
     Trigger: Customer escalates that a received item arrived cracked/torn, attaching a photo, and demands a refund.
     Flow: Maya opens the ticket → the panel auto-pulls the matching order line, fulfillment date, and return-window status → AI confirms refund eligibility against the brand's damage policy → Maya previews the partial/full refund amount → clicks Issue Refund.
     AI role: Refund-eligibility auto-check validates return window, prior refund history, and damage-policy rules; draft response generation writes an empathetic confirmation referencing the specific item and refund timeline.
     Outcome: Refund posted to Shopify, customer notified with settlement ETA, ticket closed in a single pass with a logged policy citation.
  2. Delayed-shipment status lookup
     Trigger: Customer demands to know where their order is, threatening a chargeback after 9 days of no movement.
     Flow: Maya opens the ticket → Live Order Timeline renders carrier scans, last-known location, and the 3PL exception flag → AI explains the delay cause in plain language → Maya offers a goodwill option or proactive reship.
     AI role: Sentiment-aware urgency scoring elevates the ticket; draft response generation produces a status update with carrier tracking link and an apology calibrated to delay severity.
     Outcome: Customer receives a precise, honest ETA plus optional goodwill credit; chargeback risk defused and noted in audit trail.
  3. Out-of-stock substitution offer
     Trigger: Customer wants to swap a backordered SKU for an in-stock alternative before the order ships.
     Flow: Maya opens the order → Inventory & Substitution Drawer shows live stock for similar variants ranked by size/color/price match → she selects a substitute → AI drafts the offer with price-difference handling.
     AI role: Suggested resolution path ranking surfaces the best in-stock substitutes by attribute similarity and margin; draft generation explains any price delta and credit.
     Outcome: Order line edited pre-fulfillment, substitute reserved against live inventory, customer accepts via reply — zero stockout surprise.
  4. Order modification before fulfillment
     Trigger: Customer requests address change, quantity change, or item add before the order leaves the warehouse.
     Flow: Maya opens the ticket → panel shows fulfillment status 'unfulfilled, hold window 4h' → she edits shipping address / quantity inline → system pushes a Shopify order edit and warehouse hold.
     AI role: Intent classification routes this to the modification flow; eligibility check confirms the order has not yet entered picking.
     Outcome: Order updated in Shopify, 3PL hold confirmed via webhook, customer gets a revised confirmation — no cancel-and-reorder churn.
  5. Duplicate-charge dispute
     Trigger: Customer reports being billed twice for one order and is alarmed.
     Flow: Maya opens the ticket → panel detects two transactions on the same cart token / near-identical timestamps → AI flags the duplicate authorization → Maya voids the redundant charge.
     AI role: Refund-eligibility auto-check cross-references transaction IDs and gateway authorizations to confirm a true duplicate vs. legitimate split payment.
     Outcome: Redundant charge voided/refunded in Shopify, customer reassured with transaction-level proof, finance auto-notified.
  6. Loyalty goodwill credit issuance
     Trigger: A high-LTV repeat customer has a sub-par experience and Maya wants to retain them.
     Flow: Maya opens the ticket → panel surfaces lifetime spend, order count, loyalty tier → AI recommends a credit amount within her approval limit → she issues a store credit or discount code.
     AI role: Suggested resolution path ranking weighs customer LTV and incident severity to recommend a right-sized goodwill gesture; auto-flags if amount needs lead approval.
     Outcome: Credit issued, retention gesture logged, customer sentiment recovered with a value-appropriate apology.
  7. Cross-channel ticket consolidation
     Trigger: The same customer has emailed and chatted about the same problem, creating duplicate tickets.
     Flow: Maya opens one ticket → panel detects sibling tickets by email + order match → she merges them → unified thread shows full multi-channel history.
     AI role: Embeddings-based matching links tickets by customer identity and semantic similarity of the complaint; AI summarizes the merged thread.
     Outcome: Single source of truth per incident, no contradictory replies across channels, cleaner queue.
  8. Escalation handoff to specialist
     Trigger: The case involves suspected fraud or a complex chargeback Maya can't resolve at Tier-2.
     Flow: Maya opens the ticket → AI flags fraud signals → she clicks Escalate → the system packages a structured brief with all Shopify facts and her notes for Tier-3.
     AI role: Draft generation produces a concise handoff summary; intent classification pre-tags the specialist queue.
     Outcome: Specialist receives a complete, structured case with zero re-discovery; SLA clock visibly transfers.
  9. Return-label reissue and tracking
     Trigger: Customer says their return label expired or never arrived.
     Flow: Maya opens the ticket → panel shows the original return authorization and label status → she regenerates a label inline → AI drafts the email with the new label and instructions.
     AI role: Eligibility check confirms the RMA is still within window; draft generation includes return steps and drop-off guidance.
     Outcome: Fresh label issued, return tracking visible to both parties, customer unblocked in one reply.
  10. Wrong-item-shipped correction
     Trigger: Customer received a different SKU than ordered.
     Flow: Maya opens the order → panel compares ordered vs. fulfilled line items and flags the mismatch → AI proposes reship-correct-item + keep-or-return-wrong-item path → she triggers it.
     AI role: Suggested resolution path ranking decides whether to request return of the wrong item based on its value vs. return-shipping cost.
     Outcome: Correct item reshipped against live inventory, wrong-item handling resolved, fulfillment error logged for ops review.
  11. Price-match / promo-code reconciliation
     Trigger: Customer says a promo code didn't apply or the price dropped after purchase.
     Flow: Maya opens the order → panel shows applied discounts and order timestamp vs. promo validity → AI calculates the eligible adjustment → she issues a partial refund or credit.
     AI role: Eligibility check validates the promo against order time and stacking rules; draft explains the adjustment math.
     Outcome: Fair price adjustment posted, transparent explanation sent, dispute closed.
  12. Subscription / repeat-order pause-and-credit
     Trigger: Subscription customer escalates an unwanted recurring charge.
     Flow: Maya opens the ticket → panel shows subscription schedule and last charge → she pauses the next cycle and refunds the disputed charge → AI confirms next-bill date.
     AI role: Intent classification routes to subscription flow; eligibility check confirms the charge is within refund window.
     Outcome: Subscription paused, charge refunded, customer retained without a full cancel.

KEY SCREENS (10) - every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Escalation Queue - purpose: Triage inbound escalations sorted by AI urgency score, SLA countdown, and channel, so Maya always works the right ticket next.
     Primary element: A dense, sortable ticket list with urgency heat indicators, SLA timers, and one-line AI intent summaries per row.
     Motion character: New high-urgency tickets slide in from the top with a brief amber pulse; SLA timers tick with subtle color drift toward red.
  2. Unified Customer Context Panel - purpose: The single pane that aggregates customer identity, lifetime value, order history, and active issue without any tab-switching.
     Primary element: A left identity rail (LTV, tier, contact) beside a stacked card layout of orders, refunds, and notes that hydrate progressively.
     Motion character: Cards skeleton-shimmer then settle as live Shopify data resolves, each snapping in with a 120ms stagger.
  3. Live Order Timeline - purpose: Show the full lifecycle of the relevant order — placed, paid, fulfilled, in-transit, delivered, exceptions — at a glance.
     Primary element: A vertical event timeline with carrier scan rows, exception flags, and an expandable line-item breakdown.
     Motion character: Timeline draws top-to-bottom on open; exception nodes glow and the latest scan gently pulses.
  4. Inventory & Substitution Drawer - purpose: Surface live stock for the ordered SKU and ranked in-stock substitutes for swap offers.
     Primary element: A slide-over drawer with the original variant pinned and a ranked grid of substitutes showing live quantity and price delta.
     Motion character: Drawer slides from the right; stock counts count up to live values; selected substitute lifts with a soft shadow.
  5. Refund Status Tracker - purpose: Display the true, real-time settlement state of any refund — requested, processing, settled, failed — to prevent false promises.
     Primary element: A horizontal progress stepper bound to Shopify transaction status with timestamps and gateway reference IDs.
     Motion character: The active step pulses; on settlement the stepper fills green with a single satisfying check animation.
  6. One-Click Resolution Composer - purpose: Combine the chosen resolution action and an AI-drafted customer message into a single confirm-and-send surface.
     Primary element: A split view: editable AI draft on the left, the resolution action summary (amount, SKU, address) with a primary Resolve button on the right.
     Motion character: The Resolve button breathes subtly when ready; on click, a progress ripple sweeps the action chips as each step commits.
  7. Resolution Audit Trail - purpose: Give an immutable, exportable record of every action, policy citation, and AI suggestion for compliance and lead review.
     Primary element: A reverse-chronological event log with actor, action, Shopify reference, and the policy/AI rationale attached to each entry.
     Motion character: Entries fade in newest-first; expanding an entry reveals rationale with a smooth accordion.
  8. AI Suggestion Sidebar - purpose: Persistently show the ranked resolution paths and confidence so Maya can pick or override with full reasoning visible.
     Primary element: A ranked list of 2-3 resolution cards, each with confidence, eligibility status, and a 'why' expandable.
     Motion character: Top suggestion highlights with a gentle outline; re-ranking animates cards reordering with a fluid spring.
  9. Goodwill & Approval Modal - purpose: Issue credits and route amounts above threshold to a lead approver without leaving the flow.
     Primary element: A credit-amount slider bounded by the agent's limit, with an inline approval-request state if exceeded.
     Motion character: Slider snaps to recommended value; crossing the limit flips the CTA to 'Request Approval' with a color shift.
  10. Handoff Composer - purpose: Package a complete structured case brief for Tier-3 specialists in seconds.
     Primary element: An auto-filled brief preview (summary, facts, flags, attachments) with a specialist-queue selector.
     Motion character: Fields populate in a quick cascade; the Escalate button locks the ticket with a decisive slide-out transition.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) - every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Intent classification of inbound escalation
     User action: Maya opens a ticket from the queue.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Ticket subject + body, channel, prior thread, matched Shopify order context.
     Output: A primary intent label (e.g. 'delayed-refund'), secondary tags, and the routed resolution flow.
     User benefit: She skips manual triage — the right workflow and data load instantly, shaving seconds off every ticket.
  2. Suggested resolution path ranking (headline aha)
     User action: Maya reviews the AI Suggestion Sidebar after the panel hydrates.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Intent, full Shopify order/refund/inventory state, customer LTV, brand policy ruleset, prior resolution outcomes (embeddings).
     Output: 2-3 ranked resolution cards with confidence, eligibility status, recommended amount/SKU, and a plain-language rationale.
     User benefit: The correct, policy-safe fix is pre-decided and explained — she confirms in one click instead of investigating.
  3. Refund-eligibility auto-check
     User action: Maya considers issuing a refund or credit.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Return-window dates, prior refund history, transaction IDs, damage-policy rules, promo-stacking rules.
     Output: Eligible/ineligible verdict, the maximum refundable amount, and the cited policy clause.
     User benefit: She never over-refunds or breaks policy, and never falsely promises a settlement that won't clear.
  4. Draft response generation
     User action: Maya picks a resolution path.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Resolution action details, customer sentiment, brand voice guidelines, specific order/item facts.
     Output: An empathetic, on-brand customer message referencing the exact item, amount, and timeline.
     User benefit: A polished reply is ready to send in seconds — she edits one line instead of writing from scratch.
  5. Sentiment-aware urgency scoring
     User action: Tickets arrive in the queue (background, continuous).
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Message tone, threat language ('chargeback'), LTV, SLA remaining, prior ticket count.
     Output: A 0-100 urgency score driving queue order and heat indicators.
     User benefit: She always works the most at-risk, highest-value escalation next — fewer fires turn into chargebacks.
  6. Substitute SKU matching
     User action: Maya opens the Inventory & Substitution Drawer.
     Model: Embeddings
     Input: Ordered SKU attributes (category, color, size, price, style vector), live inventory feed.
     Output: Ranked in-stock substitutes scored by attribute similarity and margin.
     User benefit: She offers swaps the customer actually wants and that are truly in stock — no bounce-backs.
  7. Cross-channel ticket linking
     User action: Maya opens a ticket that may have siblings.
     Model: Embeddings
     Input: Customer email/identity, order match, semantic similarity of complaint text across open tickets.
     Output: A surfaced list of probable duplicate tickets with merge suggestion.
     User benefit: She avoids contradictory replies and clears duplicate noise from the queue.
  8. Policy & precedent retrieval
     User action: Maya needs to justify or look up an edge-case rule.
     Model: Wiki RAG
     Input: Query against the brand's policy knowledge base and resolved-case precedents.
     Output: The relevant policy clause and a similar past resolution, cited.
     User benefit: She handles edge cases confidently with the exact rule at hand, and the citation lands in the audit trail.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: Data-dense operational restraint — Stripe-grade console clarity meets calm trustworthiness; monochrome base with a single confident accent and status-driven color used sparingly and meaningfully.
  Hero treatment: The Unified Context Panel as a living dashboard: a quiet neutral canvas where structured cards hydrate with real Shopify data, status colors (amber processing, green settled, red exception) carry semantic weight, and the AI sidebar reads as a trusted advisor rather than a chatbot. Density is legible, never cluttered — generous whitespace between dense modules.
  Motion character: Purposeful and physics-grounded: staggered card hydration that feels like data arriving, spring-based re-ranking, progress ripples that mirror real backend commits, and a single celebratory check on resolution. Motion confirms system truth — never decorative.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these - the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. Product thumbnails for inventory variants and substitution cards (apparel flat-lays on neutral seamless background, soft studio lighting)
    2. Customer-attached damage photos for damaged-item tickets (realistic cracked mug / torn jacket, casual phone-photo aesthetic)
    3. Empty-state illustration for a cleared queue (minimal line-art, calming, 'all caught up' tone)
    4. Carrier/shipping iconography set for the Live Order Timeline (clean monochrome line icons for scan, transit, delivery, exception)

FEATURE ROADMAP (3 phases) - the prototype demonstrates Phase 1 in working code; later phases appear as roadmap surfaces inside the experience:
  1. Phase 1 (Weeks 1-3) - Foundations — Single Pane
     • Escalation Queue with SLA timers and channel filtering
     • Unified Customer Context Panel hydrating order + customer + refund data from Shopify Admin API
     • Live Order Timeline with carrier scans and exception flags
     • Refund Status Tracker bound to real transaction settlement state
     • Read-only audit trail logging every panel view
     • Auth + role scoping (agent vs. lead)
     Success: Median context-assembly time per ticket drops from 4+ min to under 30 seconds; zero tab-switches needed for the top-5 escalation types.
  2. Phase 2 (Month 2) - Intelligence — Suggest & Resolve
     • Intent classification and sentiment-aware urgency scoring driving queue order
     • Suggested resolution path ranking sidebar with confidence + rationale
     • Refund-eligibility auto-check against policy ruleset
     • Draft response generation in brand voice
     • One-Click Resolution Composer committing refund/credit/edit actions to Shopify
     • Inventory & Substitution Drawer with embeddings-based SKU matching
     Success: ≥60% of eligible tickets resolved in one pass with AI-drafted reply; first-contact resolution rate up 25%; re-open rate from false refund promises near zero.
  3. Phase 3 (Quarter 2) - Scale — Consolidate & Govern
     • Cross-channel ticket linking and merge
     • Goodwill & Approval flow with threshold routing to leads
     • Handoff Composer producing structured Tier-3 briefs
     • Policy & precedent retrieval (Wiki RAG) with citations in audit trail
     • Multi-provider AI fallback (Gemini → Claude) for resilience
     • Lead analytics dashboard: AHT, FCR, AI-acceptance, refund accuracy
     Success: Average handle time down 35% vs. baseline; AI suggestion acceptance ≥70%; 100% of resolutions carry a logged policy citation.

NARRATIVE ARC (6 beats) - the multi-timeframe user journey the prototype must SUGGEST through copy, seed data, and roadmap surfaces:
  1. Minute 1
     User: Maya logs in and opens the top ticket — an angry delayed-refund escalation — and the whole customer story is already on screen.
     AI: Intent classification has tagged it, urgency scoring put it first, and the eligibility check has the refund verdict ready.
     Feeling: Relief — no scramble across tabs; the case is already understood.
  2. Minute 5
     User: She clicks the top AI resolution, edits one sentence of the draft, and hits Resolve; refund issues and the email sends.
     AI: Draft generation wrote an empathetic reply citing the exact jacket and settlement ETA; the composer commits the Shopify refund.
     Feeling: Confidence — she fixed it correctly and the customer got a real answer, not a hollow promise.
  3. Day 1
     User: By end of shift Maya has cleared 47 tickets instead of her usual 38, with no re-opens from refund lag.
     AI: The system surfaced substitutes that were actually in stock and pre-checked every eligibility decision.
     Feeling: Capable — the tooling finally keeps pace with her.
  4. Week 1
     User: She trusts the AI suggestions enough to accept most on sight, reserving judgment for edge cases the sidebar flags.
     AI: Precedent retrieval starts surfacing how similar cases were resolved, accelerating her edge-case decisions.
     Feeling: Trust — the recommendations have earned it.
  5. Month 1
     User: Maya handles cross-channel duplicates and goodwill credits inline; her lead reviews a clean audit trail instead of chasing her for context.
     AI: Ticket linking de-duplicates the queue and every action carries a policy citation automatically.
     Feeling: Pride — her work is auditable, consistent, and fast.
  6. Month 3+
     User: Maya is now the team's go-to for tricky escalations because ResolveDesk lets her resolve them confidently; AHT is down a third team-wide.
     AI: Multi-provider fallback keeps suggestions flowing even during a provider outage; analytics show 70%+ AI acceptance.
     Feeling: Mastery — the console amplifies her judgment rather than replacing it.

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (10 beats) - the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Maya clicks the top delayed-refund ticket in the Escalation Queue.
     System: Workspace transitions to the Unified Context Panel; identity rail appears instantly with skeleton cards for orders and refunds.
     Motion/feedback: Queue row lifts and slides left as the panel wipes in from the right. (250ms)
  2. She waits a beat as data loads.
     System: Shopify order, customer LTV, and refund records hydrate; skeleton shimmer resolves into real values card by card.
     Motion/feedback: Each card snaps in with a 120ms stagger and a subtle fade. (1400ms)
  3. Her eye goes to the Refund Status Tracker.
     System: The stepper shows the refund is stuck at 'processing' since 8 days ago — the real reason for the customer's anger.
     Motion/feedback: The 'processing' step pulses amber to draw attention. (300ms)
  4. She glances at the AI Suggestion Sidebar.
     System: Top card reads 'Re-trigger settled refund + apology credit', confidence 0.93, with eligibility confirmed and rationale expandable.
     Motion/feedback: Top suggestion outlines with a gentle highlight; lower cards settle beneath it. (400ms)
  5. Maya expands the 'why' on the top suggestion.
     System: Rationale shows the gateway refund failed silently; policy POL-104 permits a $10 goodwill credit for delays over 5 days.
     Motion/feedback: Accordion expands smoothly; the cited policy link glows. (250ms)
  6. She clicks 'Use this resolution'.
     System: One-Click Resolution Composer opens with the AI-drafted reply on the left and action chips (Re-issue refund $128, +$10 credit) on the right.
     Motion/feedback: Composer slides up; the Resolve button breathes softly to signal readiness. (300ms)
  7. Maya edits one sentence to add a personal touch.
     System: Draft updates live; character/tone indicator stays green for brand voice.
     Motion/feedback: Inline edit with no reflow jank; tone meter holds steady. (200ms)
  8. She clicks Resolve.
     System: A progress ripple sweeps the action chips: refund re-issued to Shopify → credit applied → email sent → ticket closed.
     Motion/feedback: Each chip flips to a green check in sequence as it commits. (1600ms)
  9. Maya watches confirmation.
     System: Refund Status Tracker fills green to 'settled'; a toast confirms 'Resolved — customer notified'.
     Motion/feedback: Single satisfying check animation on the stepper; toast slides in then fades. (700ms)
  10. She moves on.
     System: Audit Trail logs every action with actor, Shopify refs, and the POL-104 citation; queue auto-advances to the next highest-urgency ticket.
     Motion/feedback: Resolved ticket animates out of the queue; next ticket rises to the top with a brief amber pulse. (400ms)
